substantive_reconstruction.exact_model: Let J†J=I,P=JJ†,R=2P-I and J†UJ=A. Then ||A||≤1 follows from unitary compression and does not silently restrict an arbitrary separately scaled target. Choose complete orthonormal SVD bases Av_i=σ_i w_i,A†w_i=σ_i v_i with0≤σ_i≤1, no normality/diagonalizability. Unit singular vectors are proof bases, not an additional normalized arbitrary-input premise.
substantive_reconstruction.directed_companions: For σ<1 put p=Jv,p'=Jw,s=sqrt(1-σ²),q=(U†p'-σp)/s,q'=(Up-σp')/s. Compression of U/U† makes both whole clean projections zero; unitarity gives norm1. Up=σp'+sq',Uq=sp'-σq'; U†p'=σp+sq,U†q'=sp-σq. Thus U:H→H' and U†:H'→H have directed Sσ matrices. Applying U again is not the guaranteed reverse and planes need not be distinct.
substantive_reconstruction.full_leakage_actions: R is Z on both ordered bases. E=U†RUR has Mσ² on H and extra UR has Mσ from H to H', where Mσ=[[σ,-s],[s,σ]]. Hence E^k p=T2k(σ)p+sU_(2k-1)(σ)q for k≥1, while UR E^k p=T_(2k+1)(σ)p'+sU_(2k)(σ)q' for k≥0. Upper-right matrix entry has negative sign, first-column leakage positive. E0=I directly. These are full vector equations; deleting leakage before taking the clean projection would be false.
substantive_reconstruction.extra_reflection_is_material: The extra odd map is UR, not arbitrary U. For canonical Hermitian dilation U=[[t,s],[s,-t]]⊗I2 with t=1/2, E=M². UE on a clean basis vector has clean coefficient+1/2, while UR E has coefficient-1=T3(1/2); this independently shows that the extra R cannot be dropped when k>0. For k0, RJ=J explains why the degree1 compression still equals A.
substantive_reconstruction.projected_assembly: Applying J† kills q/q'. On every right singular basis vector, the even compression acts as T2k(σ_i)v_i and the odd as T_(2k+1)(σ_i)w_i. Completeness yields V T2k(Σ)V† and W T_(2k+1)(Σ)V†. Thus the even input/output clean side is right/right, while the final directed odd step changes the output to the left basis; this is alternating U/U† parity, not a universal each-U swap rule.
substantive_reconstruction.zero_one_and_basis_choices: σ0 has s1, so companions are well-defined; T_odd(0)=0 and T_even(0)=(-1)^k. σ1 has zero leakage: Up=p',U†p'=p,E p=p,UR E^k p=p', without defining zero/s companions or asserting p=p'. Repeated nonzero singular bases transform together; null bases may be chosen independently. Because T2k(x)=h_k(x²), even output=h_k(A†A); because T_(2k+1)(x)=x g_k(x²), odd output=A g_k(A†A). This proves basis independence including arbitrary left kernel choices. A0 gives even(-1)^k I and odd0, not a normalized zero state.
